subtype: Approach: padding with copied tutorial projects [Pitfall]
passage:
Santosh: interview went badly
Tarun: what happened?
Santosh: he opened my portfolio. To-do app, weather app, calculator. Asked why I chose a database for the to-do app
Tarun: and?
Santosh: I froze. I followed a video for it. I couldn't say why
Santosh: he asked about the calculator too. Same. I copied every one
Tarun: ouch
Santosh: he said politely "thank you for showing your work" but I saw his face change. I think he stopped trusting the rest of my list
Tarun: what will you do?
Santosh: build one thing I can explain line by line. Not another clone

qa.q: Which three apps were in Santosh's portfolio?
qa.a: There were a to-do app, a weather app and a calculator.

qa.q: What is Santosh feeling after the interview?
qa.a: Santosh feels embarrassed and shaken, describing freezing when asked why, and worries that the interviewer stopped trusting the list.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Santosh use to build the portfolio, and why?
qa.a: Santosh could build one project around a real need and keep notes on each choice, because being able to explain decisions matters more than the number of apps.

qa.q: How might the interviewer have seen the portfolio?
qa.a: The interviewer saw three familiar apps and could not learn how Santosh thinks, so trust in the rest of the list dropped after the questions.

grounding: Shows padding a portfolio with copied tutorial projects and being unable to defend the choices in an interview.
